SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Respondent maintains that the learned Deputy High Court Judge was correct to find that the statutory defence under section 58 of the Highways Act 1980 had been established. The inspection system was reasonable and the hole was not present at the time of the February 2020 inspection. There was no common law duty to erect signage as alleged.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Respondent is the highway authority responsible for the grass verge, footway and carriageway where the Appellant fell on 22 April 2020.
A routine highway inspection was conducted on 13 February 2020 by Mr Cooke, an experienced safety inspector.
The hole was very likely not present on 13 February 2020 and developed shortly before the accident, probably due to animal burrowing activity.
The hole varied in size over short periods, not being detected on 6 October 2020 but being present again on 30 October 2020.
The Appellant was travelling at approximately 10mph and made a sharp right turn onto the verge to overtake a jogger.
The general presumption is that paths cannot be used for cycling absent express permission; no shared use signs were present north of the Paul Cully bridge.

Contentions.item: The Respondent established the statutory defence under section 58 of the Highways Act 1980 by demonstrating reasonable care in highway maintenance.
The inspection system as a whole was reasonable and the February 2020 inspection was competent.
The hole was not present at the time of the inspection and developed subsequently due to animal activity.
There is no common law duty on a highway authority to erect signage; a failure to erect a sign is an omission or non-feasance which does not give rise to liability.
The Appellant's speed of 10mph was excessive for the conditions and his sharp right-hand turn made it difficult to see the route ahead.
If liability is established, the judge's finding of 33% contributory negligence should be increased.

LegalBasis.item: Highways Act 1980, Section 41 (duty to maintain highways)
Common law principles regarding omissions and non-feasance

ReliefSought.item: Dismiss the appeal and uphold the lower court's decision.
In the alternative, if the appeal is allowed, increase the finding of contributory negligence beyond 33%.
